misconceptions.description: Swaps the sides opposite and adjacent to an angle.

flashcard.front: In a right triangle, which side is adjacent to an angle?
flashcard.back: The side that touches the angle and isn't the hypotenuse. The opposite side is across from it.

misconceptions.description: Calls the hypotenuse the adjacent side.

flashcard.front: Is the hypotenuse ever 'adjacent'?
flashcard.back: No: the hypotenuse is the longest side, opposite the right angle.

misconceptions.description: Uses sin for cos (or the reverse).

flashcard.front: sin θ or cos θ: which uses the side adjacent to θ?
flashcard.back: cos θ = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse; sin θ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse.

misconceptions.description: Writes a trigonometric ratio upside down.

flashcard.front: Is sin θ = hypotenuse ÷ opposite?
flashcard.back: No: sin θ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse (always at most 1).

misconceptions.description: Classifies a terminating decimal or a fraction as irrational (or the reverse).

flashcard.front: Is 22/7 irrational?
flashcard.back: No: it is a ratio of integers. √2 is irrational.

misconceptions.description: Subtracts the magnitudes when finding the distance from a negative to a positive number.

flashcard.front: Distance from −3 to 5 on a number line?

misconceptions.description: Multiplies distance by speed to get time.

flashcard.front: Time from distance and speed?
flashcard.back: time = distance ÷ speed.

misconceptions.description: Divides speed by distance for time.

flashcard.front: Units check: km ÷ (km/h) gives?
flashcard.back: hours: so time = d ÷ v.

misconceptions.description: Divides the change in x by the change in y.

flashcard.front: Slope of a line?
flashcard.back: Rise ÷ run: Δy ÷ Δx.

misconceptions.description: Judges steepness by the signed slope rather than its size.

flashcard.front: Which is steeper: slope −3 or slope 2?
flashcard.back: Slope −3: steepness is |m|.

misconceptions.description: Uses the height at one end for the area under a sloping line.

flashcard.front: Area under a sloping straight line?
flashcard.back: A trapezium: ½(y₁ + y₂) × width.

misconceptions.description: Forgets the ½ in the area of a triangle.

flashcard.front: Area of a triangle?
flashcard.back: ½ × base × height.

misconceptions.description: Changes the sign wrongly when moving a term across the equals sign.

flashcard.front: Solve 3x + 4 = 19.
flashcard.back: Subtract 4 from both sides first: 3x = 15, x = 5.

misconceptions.description: Divides before removing the added term.

flashcard.front: ax + b = c: first step?
flashcard.back: Subtract b from both sides, then divide by a.

misconceptions.description: Keeps the wrong sign when making a variable the subject.

flashcard.front: Make a the subject of v = u + at.
flashcard.back: a = (v − u) ÷ t.

misconceptions.description: Multiplies instead of dividing when isolating a variable.

flashcard.front: Undo multiplying by t?
flashcard.back: Divide both sides by t.

misconceptions.description: Takes the roots of x² − (p + q)x + pq = 0 as −p and −q.

flashcard.front: Roots of (x − p)(x − q) = 0?
flashcard.back: x = p and x = q.

misconceptions.description: Uses b² + 4ac for the discriminant.

flashcard.front: Discriminant of ax² + bx + c?
flashcard.back: b² − 4ac.

misconceptions.description: Forgets to square b in the discriminant.

flashcard.front: Discriminant?
flashcard.back: b² − 4ac.

misconceptions.description: Adds the horizontal and vertical gaps for a distance.

flashcard.front: Distance between two points?
flashcard.back: √(Δx² + Δy²).

misconceptions.description: Halves the difference of the coordinates instead of averaging them.

flashcard.front: Midpoint x-coordinate?
flashcard.back: (x₁ + x₂) ÷ 2.

misconceptions.description: Uses 360° as the angle sum of a triangle.

flashcard.front: Angles of a triangle add to?

misconceptions.description: Thinks alternate angles add to 180°.

flashcard.front: Alternate angles between parallel lines?
flashcard.back: Equal.

misconceptions.description: Adds the two shorter sides to get the hypotenuse.

flashcard.front: Hypotenuse from legs a and b?
flashcard.back: √(a² + b²).

misconceptions.description: Adds the squares when finding a shorter side.

flashcard.front: Shorter side from c and a?
flashcard.back: √(c² − a²).

misconceptions.description: Uses degrees in s = rθ.

flashcard.front: Arc length s = rθ: θ in?
flashcard.back: Radians.

misconceptions.description: Uses the circumference formula for the area of a circle.

flashcard.front: Area of a circle?
flashcard.back: πr² (2πr is the circumference).

misconceptions.description: Uses the diameter in πr².

flashcard.front: Area of a circle of diameter d?

misconceptions.description: Believes a steady force keeps a body moving at constant speed on a frictionless surface.

flashcard.front: Unbalanced force on a body: effect?
flashcard.back: It accelerates: speeds up, slows down or turns.

misconceptions.description: Treats mass and weight as the same quantity.

flashcard.front: On the Moon, which stays the same: mass or weight?
flashcard.back: Mass. Weight (mg) depends on g.

misconceptions.description: Divides force by distance for work.

flashcard.front: Work done by a force F moving its point d along itself?
flashcard.back: W = F × d.

misconceptions.description: Thinks energy disappears as a ball falls.

flashcard.front: A falling ball loses height. Where does the energy go?
flashcard.back: Into kinetic energy (and a little into heat with air resistance).

misconceptions.description: Uses cos θ = 1 − sin θ.

flashcard.front: From sin θ to cos θ?
flashcard.back: cos θ = √(1 − sin²θ) for an acute angle.

misconceptions.description: Forgets the square root in cos θ = √(1 − sin²θ).

flashcard.front: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 gives cos θ = ?
flashcard.back: √(1 − sin²θ).

misconceptions.description: Swaps the standard values of sin 30° and sin 60°.

flashcard.front: sin 30°?

misconceptions.description: Gives the total distance travelled when asked for displacement.

flashcard.front: Is displacement the total distance travelled?
flashcard.back: No. Displacement is the change in position (final − initial), with a direction; path length is the total distance covered.

misconceptions.description: Gives the change in position when asked for the distance travelled.

flashcard.front: A walk out and back: is the path length the same as the displacement?
flashcard.back: No. Path length adds every stretch travelled; displacement only compares the start and end.

misconceptions.description: Drops the sign (direction) of a displacement.

flashcard.front: Can a displacement be negative?
flashcard.back: Yes. Its sign gives its direction along the axis: negative means towards −x.

misconceptions.description: Uses only the last stretch of a journey as the displacement.

flashcard.front: Displacement for a two-stage journey?
flashcard.back: Final position minus initial position, not just the last stage.

misconceptions.description: Divides metres by minutes and reports the result as m/s.

flashcard.front: Distance in m, time in min: is d ÷ t in m/s?
flashcard.back: No. Convert minutes to seconds first (× 60).

misconceptions.description: Averages two speeds arithmetically when equal distances are covered at each.

flashcard.front: Half the distance at v₁, half at v₂: average speed?
flashcard.back: 2v₁v₂ ÷ (v₁ + v₂), not (v₁ + v₂) ÷ 2: more time is spent at the slower speed.

misconceptions.description: Uses total distance ÷ time when average velocity is asked.

flashcard.front: Average velocity or average speed: which uses displacement?
flashcard.back: Average velocity = displacement ÷ time; average speed = path length ÷ time.

misconceptions.description: Averages the velocities of the stages instead of dividing displacement by total time.

flashcard.front: Is average velocity the mean of the stage velocities?
flashcard.back: Only if the stages take equal times. In general, total displacement ÷ total time.

misconceptions.description: Reads a negative x–t slope as slowing down.

flashcard.front: A straight x–t line sloping down: what is happening?
flashcard.back: Constant velocity in the −x direction. Slope is velocity; a straight line means it doesn't change.

misconceptions.description: Reads a position–time graph as a picture of the path.

flashcard.front: Is an x–t graph a picture of the route?
flashcard.back: No. It shows position against time; its slope is the velocity.

misconceptions.description: Divides one position by one time instead of using the change in position.

flashcard.front: Velocity from an x–t line?
flashcard.back: Slope = Δx ÷ Δt between two points, not x ÷ t at one point.

misconceptions.description: Uses run over rise for a slope.

flashcard.front: Slope of a straight-line graph?
flashcard.back: Rise over run: change in the vertical quantity ÷ change in the horizontal one.

misconceptions.description: Uses the average velocity from t = 0 instead of the tangent's slope.

flashcard.front: Instantaneous velocity on a curved x–t graph?
flashcard.back: The slope of the tangent at that instant, not x ÷ t.

misconceptions.description: Reads the position at an instant as the velocity.

flashcard.front: On an x–t graph, is the height of the curve the velocity?
flashcard.back: No. The height is the position; the slope is the velocity.

misconceptions.description: Uses v ÷ t for acceleration, ignoring the initial velocity.

flashcard.front: Acceleration from u to v in time t?
flashcard.back: a = (v − u) ÷ t: the change in velocity per unit time.

misconceptions.description: Adds the velocities instead of subtracting them.

flashcard.front: Is acceleration (u + v) ÷ t?
flashcard.back: No: (v − u) ÷ t.

misconceptions.description: Multiplies the final velocity by the whole time.

flashcard.front: Displacement from a v–t graph?
flashcard.back: The area under it: a sloping part makes a triangle or trapezium, not a rectangle of height v.

misconceptions.description: Leaves out the accelerating part of the v–t area.

flashcard.front: v–t graph: acceleration phase then constant speed. Distance?
flashcard.back: Triangle (acceleration) + rectangle (constant speed).

misconceptions.description: Leaves the initial velocity out of v = u + at.

flashcard.front: v = u + at: what does u add?
flashcard.back: The velocity the body already had; a t is only the change.

misconceptions.description: Leaves out the distance covered during the reaction time.

flashcard.front: Stopping distance with a reaction time?
flashcard.back: Thinking distance u·t_r plus braking distance u² ÷ 2a.

misconceptions.description: Drops the ½ in v² = u² + 2as (or s = ut + ½at²).

flashcard.front: Braking distance from u at deceleration a?
flashcard.back: u² ÷ (2a): the 2 comes from v² = u² + 2as.

misconceptions.description: Gives the distance fallen when the speed is asked.

flashcard.front: Speed after falling for t seconds from rest?
flashcard.back: v = g t (the distance is ½ g t²).

misconceptions.description: Gives the time to the top when the height is asked.

flashcard.front: Maximum height of a ball thrown up at u?
flashcard.back: u² ÷ (2g); the time to the top is u ÷ g.

misconceptions.description: Uses the time to return to the launch height when the ball lands lower.

flashcard.front: Ball thrown up from a cliff top: time to the ground below?
flashcard.back: Solve h + ut − ½gt² = 0 with the cliff height; 2u/g only brings it back to the top.

misconceptions.description: Treats a thrown ball as simply dropped.

flashcard.front: Thrown up from a cliff vs dropped: same time to land?
flashcard.back: No. The upward throw adds time going up and coming back.

misconceptions.description: Adds the velocities of bodies moving the same way.

flashcard.front: Velocity of A relative to B, both moving the same way?
flashcard.back: v_A − v_B.

misconceptions.description: Subtracts speeds of bodies approaching each other.

flashcard.front: Two cars approaching head-on: closing speed?
flashcard.back: The sum of their speeds.

misconceptions.description: Uses only one train's length for an overtaking time.

flashcard.front: Time for one train to pass another completely?
flashcard.back: (L₁ + L₂) ÷ relative speed.

misconceptions.description: Adds the speeds of trains moving the same way.

flashcard.front: Relative speed of trains moving the same way?
flashcard.back: The difference of their speeds.

misconceptions.description: Uses only u·t for the distance, ignoring the speed gained.

flashcard.front: Is the distance u × t when the body speeds up?
flashcard.back: No. Add the triangle ½(v − u)t for the speed gained.

misconceptions.description: Uses only the triangle above the starting speed.

flashcard.front: Area under a sloping v–t line from u to v?
flashcard.back: A rectangle u·t plus a triangle ½(v − u)t.

misconceptions.description: Uses the slope of a v–t graph when the area is asked.

flashcard.front: What does the area under a v–t graph give?
flashcard.back: The displacement. The slope gives the acceleration.

misconceptions.description: Drops the ½ in the braking-distance formula.

flashcard.front: Braking distance from u at deceleration a?

misconceptions.description: Uses u instead of u² in the braking-distance formula.

flashcard.front: Double the speed: braking distance?
flashcard.back: Four times as large: s = u² ÷ (2a).

misconceptions.description: Gives the stopping time u ÷ a when the distance is asked.

flashcard.front: Stopping time or stopping distance: u ÷ a or u² ÷ (2a)?
flashcard.back: u ÷ a is the time; u² ÷ (2a) is the distance.

misconceptions.description: Assumes the normal force always equals mg, including on an incline or when other forces have perpendicular components.

flashcard.front: On a 30° incline, is the normal force on a resting block equal to its weight?
flashcard.back: No. The normal force balances only the component of weight perpendicular to the surface: N = mg cos θ (when nothing else pushes into the surface).

misconceptions.description: Uses mg sin θ for the perpendicular component and mg cos θ for the component along the incline.

flashcard.front: Which component of weight acts along a slope of angle θ?
flashcard.back: mg sin θ along the slope; mg cos θ perpendicular to it. The angle between the weight and the perpendicular to the slope equals θ.

misconceptions.description: Adds a 'force of motion' or 'force of the push' that has no agent after contact has ended.

flashcard.front: A box slides after you stop pushing. Is your push still a force on it?
flashcard.back: No. Every force needs an agent in contact (or a field). The box keeps moving because of inertia, and friction slows it.

misconceptions.description: Sets static friction equal to μs·N even when a smaller force would keep the body at rest.

flashcard.front: Is static friction always μs N?
flashcard.back: No. μs N is the maximum. Static friction is only as large as needed to prevent slipping, up to that maximum.

misconceptions.description: Points friction opposite the applied force rather than opposite the (tendency of) relative motion.

flashcard.front: Friction opposes what, exactly?
flashcard.back: Relative motion (or the tendency of relative motion) between the surfaces in contact, not necessarily the applied force.

misconceptions.description: Treats weight and normal force as a Newton's third law pair acting on the same body.

flashcard.front: Are weight and normal force on a book an action–reaction pair?
flashcard.back: No. Third-law pairs act on different bodies and are the same type of interaction. The pair of the book's weight is the book's pull on the Earth.

misconceptions.description: Answer has units of a different physical quantity (e.g. kg instead of N).

flashcard.front: Weight in newtons or kilograms?
flashcard.back: Mass is in kg; weight is a force, W = mg, in newtons.

misconceptions.description: Treats the whole weight as acting along a slope.

flashcard.front: Does all of a block's weight pull it down a slope?
flashcard.back: No. Only W sin θ acts along the slope; W cos θ presses into it.

misconceptions.description: Resolves a horizontal push as if it acted along the incline.

flashcard.front: A horizontal push F on a θ slope: how much acts along the slope?
flashcard.back: F cos θ (and F sin θ presses into the slope).

misconceptions.description: Inverts a tangent ratio when dividing two component equations.

flashcard.front: F cos θ = mg sin θ. What is F?
flashcard.back: F = mg tan θ.

misconceptions.description: Draws unbalanced forces for a body moving at constant velocity.

flashcard.front: Constant velocity: what is the net force?
flashcard.back: Zero. All forces balance (Newton's first law).

misconceptions.description: Believes a net force is needed to keep a body moving at constant velocity.

flashcard.front: Does a body need a net force to keep moving at constant velocity?
flashcard.back: No. Zero net force means constant velocity (Newton's first law).

misconceptions.description: Multiplies force by mass to get acceleration.

flashcard.front: Net force F on mass m: acceleration?
flashcard.back: a = F ÷ m, not F × m.

misconceptions.description: Writes a = m ÷ F.

flashcard.front: Doubling the force on a body does what to its acceleration?
flashcard.back: Doubles it: a = F ÷ m.

misconceptions.description: Uses only one momentum when finding an impulse.

flashcard.front: Impulse on a bouncing ball: only the incoming momentum?
flashcard.back: No. Impulse = final momentum − initial momentum, both with signs.

misconceptions.description: Adds or subtracts momenta without signs for direction.

flashcard.front: Two carts move towards each other. Do their momenta add?
flashcard.back: They partly cancel: momentum is a vector, so give each a sign.

misconceptions.description: Expects recoiling bodies to share speeds rather than momenta.

flashcard.front: A gun fires a bullet. Do they move apart at the same speed?
flashcard.back: No. Their momenta are equal and opposite; the heavy gun moves slowly.

misconceptions.description: Confuses momentum with velocity.

flashcard.front: Momentum or velocity: which is shared equally (and oppositely) in a recoil?
flashcard.back: Momentum. Divide by each mass to find each speed.

misconceptions.description: Inverts the mass ratio in a recoil.

flashcard.front: Recoil speed of a gun of mass M firing mass m at v?
flashcard.back: V = m v ÷ M.

misconceptions.description: Averages velocities in a collision instead of conserving momentum.

flashcard.front: Two carts stick together. Is their speed the average of the two speeds?
flashcard.back: No. Use momentum: (m₁ + m₂) v = m₁u₁ + m₂u₂.

misconceptions.description: Expects a moving body to keep its speed after picking up a second body.

flashcard.front: A moving cart sticks to one at rest. Same speed afterwards?
flashcard.back: No, slower: the same momentum is shared by more mass.

misconceptions.description: Divides by only one body's mass after a sticking collision.

flashcard.front: After a sticking collision, which mass moves?
flashcard.back: Both together: m₁ + m₂.

misconceptions.description: Treats centrifugal force as a real outward force with an agent.

flashcard.front: Is there an outward 'centrifugal force' on a turning car?
flashcard.back: Not in the road's frame: no agent supplies it. The inward friction turns the car.

misconceptions.description: Thinks a force along the motion makes a body turn.

flashcard.front: Can a forward driving force make a car turn?
flashcard.back: No. A force along the motion changes speed; turning needs a force towards the centre.

misconceptions.description: Expects the vertical normal force to turn a car on a level road.

flashcard.front: On a level curve, does the normal force turn the car?
flashcard.back: No, it is vertical. Sideways friction does.

misconceptions.description: Stops at v² and forgets the square root.

flashcard.front: μ g r for a level bend gives what?
flashcard.back: v², the square of the greatest speed. Take the square root.

misconceptions.description: Ignores the friction limit when finding the greatest speed on a level bend.

flashcard.front: What limits the speed on a level bend?
flashcard.back: Friction: v_max = √(μ g r).

misconceptions.description: Uses sin θ instead of tan θ for a frictionless banked curve.

flashcard.front: Banked curve, no friction: which trig ratio links v and θ?
flashcard.back: tan θ = v² ÷ (r g).

misconceptions.description: Pairs a gravitational force with a contact force as a third-law pair.

flashcard.front: The partner of a gravitational force is…?
flashcard.back: Another gravitational force, on the other body.

misconceptions.description: Believes third-law pairs need motion.

flashcard.front: Do third-law pairs need motion?
flashcard.back: No: any interaction between two bodies gives a pair.

misconceptions.description: Uses the mass where the weight (a force) is needed.

flashcard.front: Kinetic friction on a crate of mass m on a level floor?
flashcard.back: μ_k m g: μ times the normal force, a force in newtons.

misconceptions.description: Sets a horizontal rope's tension equal to the weight.

flashcard.front: A horizontal rope drags a crate at constant speed. What does the tension balance?
flashcard.back: Kinetic friction, not the weight.

misconceptions.description: Divides the net force by only one of the connected masses.

flashcard.front: A pull on A drags B by a string. Which mass sets the acceleration?
flashcard.back: The total m_A + m_B.

misconceptions.description: Expects masses on a pulley to fall freely with acceleration g.

flashcard.front: Do the masses on a pulley fall with acceleration g?
flashcard.back: No: a = (m₁ − m₂) g ÷ (m₁ + m₂), less than g.

misconceptions.description: Ranks accelerations by force alone.

flashcard.front: Bigger force, bigger acceleration?
flashcard.back: Only for the same mass: a = F ÷ m.

misconceptions.description: Leaves friction out of a diagram for a body sliding on a rough surface.

flashcard.front: A box pulled at constant speed on a rough floor: what balances the pull?
flashcard.back: Kinetic friction from the floor, opposite the motion.

misconceptions.description: Ranks accelerations ignoring the masses.

flashcard.front: Cart X: 8 N on 4 kg. Cart Y: 6 N on 2 kg. Which accelerates faster?
flashcard.back: Y: 3 m/s² against 2 m/s². Compare F/m, not F alone.

misconceptions.description: Ranks accelerations ignoring the forces.

flashcard.front: Does the lightest cart always accelerate fastest?
flashcard.back: No. a = F/m: a larger force can beat a smaller mass.

misconceptions.description: Pairs two forces from different interactions as a third-law pair.

flashcard.front: What do the two forces of a third-law pair have in common?
flashcard.back: Same interaction and type, equal size, opposite directions, acting on the two different bodies.

misconceptions.description: Thinks the heavier body exerts the larger force in an interaction.

flashcard.front: In a truck–car collision, which pushes harder on the other?
flashcard.back: Neither: the forces are equal and opposite. The car accelerates more because it is lighter.

misconceptions.description: Thinks a third-law pair cancels because the forces are equal and opposite.

flashcard.front: Do the two forces of a third-law pair cancel?
flashcard.back: No. They act on different bodies.

misconceptions.description: Thinks a body released from circular motion flies radially outward.

flashcard.front: A whirled stone's string breaks. Which way does it go?
flashcard.back: Along the tangent, in a straight line: no force acts sideways any more.

misconceptions.description: Thinks a body keeps curving after the inward force stops.

flashcard.front: Does a released stone keep curving?
flashcard.back: No. With no inward force it moves in a straight line (first law).

misconceptions.description: Shares a weight equally between two angled strings as if they were vertical.

flashcard.front: Lamp hung from two strings at θ to the vertical: tension?
flashcard.back: T = W ÷ (2 cos θ): only the vertical parts hold the lamp up.

misconceptions.description: Uses sin for the component adjacent to the angle (and cos for the opposite one).

flashcard.front: Force F at θ above the x-axis: x-component?
flashcard.back: F cos θ (adjacent). The y-component is F sin θ.

misconceptions.description: Multiplies by tan θ to get a component.

flashcard.front: Does F tan θ give a component of F?
flashcard.back: No. tan θ = F_y ÷ F_x relates the components to each other.

misconceptions.description: Gives a component's size without its sign.

flashcard.front: A force points west of north. Sign of its x-component (east positive)?
flashcard.back: Negative.

misconceptions.description: Adds vector magnitudes regardless of direction.

flashcard.front: Do vector magnitudes add when the vectors are perpendicular?
flashcard.back: No. |a + b| = √(a² + b²) for perpendicular vectors.

misconceptions.description: Subtracts magnitudes for vectors that are not opposite.

flashcard.front: When does |a + b| = |a| − |b|?
flashcard.back: Only when a and b point in opposite directions.

misconceptions.description: Uses sin θ instead of sin 2θ in the range formula.

flashcard.front: Range of a projectile?
flashcard.back: R = u² sin 2θ ÷ g.

misconceptions.description: Uses the time to the top instead of the whole flight time.

flashcard.front: Is the time to the top the whole flight time?
flashcard.back: No, it's half of it (on level ground).

misconceptions.description: Uses the launch speed instead of its horizontal component.

flashcard.front: Which velocity component carries a projectile sideways?
flashcard.back: The horizontal one, u cos θ, constant without air resistance.

misconceptions.description: Treats a scalar (speed, mass, time) as a vector, or the reverse.

flashcard.front: Which needs a direction: speed or displacement?
flashcard.back: Displacement (a vector). Speed, mass and time are scalars.

misconceptions.description: Gives a negative magnitude for a vector multiplied by a negative number.

flashcard.front: Magnitude of −3a?
flashcard.back: 3|a|. The minus sign reverses the direction; a magnitude is never negative.

misconceptions.description: Uses a component of a vector as the component of its unit vector.

flashcard.front: Unit vector along a = (aₓ, a_y)?
flashcard.back: â = a ÷ |a|: divide each component by the magnitude.

misconceptions.description: Divides by the sum of the components instead of the magnitude.

flashcard.front: To make a unit vector, divide by…?
flashcard.back: The magnitude √(aₓ² + a_y²), not aₓ + a_y.

misconceptions.description: Uses √(a² + b²) for vectors that are not at right angles.

flashcard.front: Resultant of a and b at angle θ?
flashcard.back: R = √(a² + b² + 2ab cos θ); √(a² + b²) only when θ = 90°.

misconceptions.description: Uses a minus sign in the resultant formula for the angle between the vectors.

flashcard.front: Sign of 2ab cos θ in the resultant formula?
flashcard.back: Plus, when θ is the angle between a and b placed tail to tail.

misconceptions.description: Inverts the speed ratio when finding a boat's drift downstream.

flashcard.front: Drift of a boat steering straight across?
flashcard.back: drift = v_river × (width ÷ v_boat).

misconceptions.description: Uses the boat's resultant speed for the drift.

flashcard.front: Which speed carries the boat downstream?
flashcard.back: Only the river's: the crossing time is width ÷ v_boat.

misconceptions.description: Thinks a projectile is momentarily at rest at the top of its path.

flashcard.front: Velocity of a projectile at the top?
flashcard.back: Horizontal, equal to u cos θ. Only the vertical part is zero.

misconceptions.description: Thinks the velocity at the top is vertical.

flashcard.front: Direction of a projectile's velocity at the top?
flashcard.back: Horizontal.

misconceptions.description: Forgets the square root in the fall time √(2h/g).

flashcard.front: Fall time from height h?

misconceptions.description: Uses the level-ground range formula for a horizontal launch from a height.

flashcard.front: Horizontal launch from a height h: how far out does it land?
flashcard.back: x = u √(2h ÷ g); the u² sin 2θ ÷ g formula is for launch and landing at the same height.

misconceptions.description: Uses v ÷ r (the angular speed) for the centripetal acceleration.

flashcard.front: Centripetal acceleration?
flashcard.back: a = v² ÷ r (v ÷ r is ω, in rad/s).

misconceptions.description: Multiplies v² by r instead of dividing.

flashcard.front: Does a tighter turn need more or less centripetal acceleration?
flashcard.back: More: a = v² ÷ r grows as r shrinks.

misconceptions.description: Gives the speed 2πr ÷ T when the acceleration is asked.

flashcard.front: Centripetal acceleration from the period?
flashcard.back: a = 4π²r ÷ T²; 2πr ÷ T is the speed.

misconceptions.description: Scales the centripetal acceleration linearly with speed or ignores the radius.

flashcard.front: Double the speed and halve the radius: centripetal acceleration?
flashcard.back: 8 times: a ∝ v² ÷ r.

misconceptions.description: Gives the period when the frequency is asked.

flashcard.front: Frequency from period?

misconceptions.description: Gives oscillations per second when the period is asked.

flashcard.front: n oscillations in t seconds: period?
flashcard.back: T = t ÷ n.

misconceptions.description: Uses the difference of the periods as the time to be in phase again.

flashcard.front: Two pendulums T₁ < T₂: next time in phase?
flashcard.back: When the faster one has made one extra oscillation: T₁T₂ ÷ (T₂ − T₁).

misconceptions.description: Uses sin φ for x(0) when x = A cos(ωt + φ).

flashcard.front: x = A cos(ωt + φ): x at t = 0?
flashcard.back: A cos φ.

misconceptions.description: Gives the amplitude as the displacement at an instant.

flashcard.front: Is x(0) always A?
flashcard.back: Only if φ = 0: x(0) = A cos φ.

misconceptions.description: Uses cos(t ÷ T) instead of cos(2πt ÷ T).

flashcard.front: x(t) with period T?
flashcard.back: A cos(2πt ÷ T) (ω = 2π ÷ T).

misconceptions.description: Uses the inverse sine to find a phase in x = A cos(ωt + φ).

flashcard.front: x(0) = A cos φ: φ = ?
flashcard.back: cos⁻¹(x₀ ÷ A), with its sign set by the direction of motion.

misconceptions.description: Ignores the direction of motion when choosing the phase.

flashcard.front: Two phases give the same x(0). How to choose?
flashcard.back: Use the velocity: v(0) = −Aω sin φ.

misconceptions.description: Mixes up Aω (maximum speed) and Aω² (maximum acceleration).

flashcard.front: Maximum speed and acceleration in SHM?
flashcard.back: v_max = Aω, a_max = Aω².

misconceptions.description: Uses ω x or ω(A − x) for the speed at x.

flashcard.front: Speed at displacement x in SHM?
flashcard.back: v = ω √(A² − x²).

misconceptions.description: Uses f instead of ω = 2πf.

flashcard.front: ω from f?
flashcard.back: ω = 2πf.

misconceptions.description: Uses centimetres in F = kx.

flashcard.front: F = kx with x in cm?
flashcard.back: Convert x to metres.

misconceptions.description: Writes T = 2π√(k ÷ m).

flashcard.front: Period of a spring–mass system?

misconceptions.description: Leaves out 2π in the spring period.

flashcard.front: T for a spring–mass system?

misconceptions.description: Mixes up the combination rules for springs.

flashcard.front: Two identical springs side by side (parallel): k_eff?
flashcard.back: 2k (in series: k/2).

misconceptions.description: Ignores the second spring.

flashcard.front: Does a second parallel spring change the period?
flashcard.back: Yes: k_eff = 2k, so T falls by √2.

misconceptions.description: Writes the energy of SHM as kA².

flashcard.front: Total energy of SHM?
flashcard.back: ½kA².

misconceptions.description: Uses A instead of A² in the energy.

flashcard.front: Double the amplitude: energy?
flashcard.back: ×4 (E = ½kA²).

misconceptions.description: Gives the potential energy when the kinetic energy is asked.

flashcard.front: KE at displacement x in SHM?
flashcard.back: ½k(A² − x²).

misconceptions.description: Thinks KE = PE at half the amplitude.

flashcard.front: Where is KE = PE in SHM?

misconceptions.description: Writes T = 2π√(g ÷ L).

flashcard.front: Period of a simple pendulum?

misconceptions.description: Leaves out the square root in the pendulum period.

flashcard.front: Quadruple L: period?
flashcard.back: Doubles: T ∝ √L.

misconceptions.description: Uses T instead of T² when solving for L.

flashcard.front: Length for a period T?
flashcard.back: L = gT² ÷ (4π²).

misconceptions.description: Expects a pendulum to swing faster where g is smaller.

flashcard.front: g six times smaller: period?
flashcard.back: √6 times longer.

misconceptions.description: Scales the period linearly with g.

flashcard.front: T depends on g how?

misconceptions.description: Puts the centre of mass at the midpoint regardless of the masses.

flashcard.front: Is the centre of mass of two unequal masses at the midpoint?
flashcard.back: No: it is nearer the heavier mass, x = (m₁x₁ + m₂x₂) ÷ (m₁ + m₂).

misconceptions.description: Measures the centre of mass from the wrong end.

flashcard.front: Centre of mass of two masses: nearer which one?
flashcard.back: The heavier one.

misconceptions.description: Averages coordinates without weighting by mass.

flashcard.front: Centre of mass of unequal masses?
flashcard.back: Weight each position by its mass: Σmx ÷ Σm.

misconceptions.description: Expects an isolated system's centre of mass to move when parts move internally.

flashcard.front: A person walks along a boat on still water. Does the centre of mass of person + boat move?
flashcard.back: No: no external horizontal force, so the boat moves back to keep it fixed.

misconceptions.description: Uses m ÷ M instead of m ÷ (m + M) for the boat's recoil.

flashcard.front: Person m walks d along boat M: boat moves?
flashcard.back: m d ÷ (m + M) backwards.

misconceptions.description: Reverses the order (and so the sign) of a cross product.

flashcard.front: î × ĵ or ĵ × î: which is +k̂?
flashcard.back: î × ĵ = k̂; ĵ × î = −k̂.

misconceptions.description: Uses cos θ for the magnitude of a cross product.

flashcard.back: |a||b| sin θ.

misconceptions.description: Multiplies magnitudes without sin θ.

flashcard.front: Cross product of parallel vectors?
flashcard.back: Zero: sin 0° = 0.

misconceptions.description: Computes a dot product when a cross product is asked.

flashcard.front: z-component of (a₁, a₂) × (b₁, b₂)?
flashcard.back: a₁b₂ − a₂b₁.

misconceptions.description: Expects the cross product of two vectors in a plane to lie in that plane.

flashcard.front: Where does a × b point for a and b in the xy-plane?
flashcard.back: Along ±z, perpendicular to both (right-hand rule).

misconceptions.description: Leaves angular speed in revolutions per second.

flashcard.front: rpm to rad/s?
flashcard.back: Multiply by 2π, divide by 60.

misconceptions.description: Forgets to convert minutes to seconds for angular speed.

flashcard.front: 1 rpm in rad/s?

misconceptions.description: Reports radians when revolutions are asked.

flashcard.front: Radians to revolutions?
flashcard.back: Divide by 2π.

misconceptions.description: Drops the ½ in θ = ω₀t + ½αt².

flashcard.front: Angle turned from rest at constant α?
flashcard.back: θ = ½αt².

misconceptions.description: Uses revolutions instead of radians in ω² = ω₀² + 2αθ.

flashcard.front: Units of θ in ω² = ω₀² + 2αθ?
flashcard.back: Radians: 1 revolution = 2π rad.

misconceptions.description: Divides force by distance for torque.

flashcard.front: Torque of F at perpendicular distance r?
flashcard.back: τ = F r.

misconceptions.description: Inverts the mass ratio when balancing a see-saw.

flashcard.front: Where must the heavier child sit to balance?
flashcard.back: Closer to the pivot: m₁d₁ = m₂d₂.

misconceptions.description: Expects unequal masses to balance at equal distances.

flashcard.front: Do unequal weights balance at equal distances?
flashcard.back: No: the moments m g d must be equal.

misconceptions.description: Measures the beam's weight arm from the end instead of from the pivot.

flashcard.front: Moment arm of a uniform beam's weight?
flashcard.back: From the pivot to the beam's centre.

misconceptions.description: Ignores the weight of the beam itself.

flashcard.front: Does a uniform beam's own weight have a moment about an off-centre pivot?
flashcard.back: Yes: its weight acts at the centre.

misconceptions.description: Uses MR² (a ring) for a uniform disc.

flashcard.front: Moment of inertia of a uniform disc about its axis?
flashcard.back: ½MR².

misconceptions.description: Forgets the square root in k = √(I ÷ M).

flashcard.front: Radius of gyration?

misconceptions.description: Uses half the rod's length as its radius of gyration.

flashcard.front: Radius of gyration of a rod about its centre?

misconceptions.description: Uses m r instead of m r² for moment of inertia.

flashcard.front: Moment of inertia of point masses?
flashcard.back: Σ m r².

misconceptions.description: Puts all the mass at the centre of mass when computing I.

flashcard.front: Can you use the centre of mass for I?
flashcard.back: No: I = Σ m r² depends on where each mass is.

misconceptions.description: Multiplies torque by moment of inertia for angular acceleration.

flashcard.front: Angular acceleration from τ and I?
flashcard.back: α = τ ÷ I.

misconceptions.description: Writes rotational KE as Iω².

flashcard.front: Rotational kinetic energy?
flashcard.back: ½Iω².

misconceptions.description: Treats a heavy pulley as massless.

flashcard.front: A mass hangs from a cord round a heavy disc pulley: is a = g?
flashcard.back: No: a = mg ÷ (m + M/2).

misconceptions.description: Uses MR² for a disc-shaped pulley.

flashcard.front: Disc pulley's effective mass in a = mg ÷ (m + …)?
flashcard.back: M/2, from I = ½MR².

misconceptions.description: Uses ½Iω² for angular momentum.

flashcard.front: Angular momentum?
flashcard.back: L = Iω.

misconceptions.description: Divides I by ω for angular momentum.

flashcard.front: Units of angular momentum?
flashcard.back: kg m²/s: L = Iω.

misconceptions.description: Inverts the ratio when angular momentum is conserved.

flashcard.front: Skater pulls in arms (I falls): ω?
flashcard.back: Rises: ω₂ = I₁ω₁ ÷ I₂.

misconceptions.description: Averages angular velocities when two bodies start rotating together.

flashcard.front: Two discs coupled: final ω?
flashcard.back: I₁ω₁ ÷ (I₁ + I₂), from conservation of angular momentum.

misconceptions.description: Conserves rotational KE in a sticking (coupling) process.

flashcard.front: Is rotational KE conserved when two discs couple?
flashcard.back: No: angular momentum is conserved; KE is lost.

misconceptions.description: Uses run over rise for a slope.

flashcard.front: Slope of a line?
flashcard.back: Rise over run: Δy ÷ Δx.

misconceptions.description: Gets the sign of the y-intercept wrong.

flashcard.front: y = mx + c: where does the line cross the y-axis?

misconceptions.description: Uses equal slopes for perpendicular lines.

flashcard.front: Slopes of perpendicular lines?
flashcard.back: They multiply to −1.

misconceptions.description: Flips a slope for a perpendicular line but keeps its sign.

flashcard.front: A line has slope 2/3. Slope of a perpendicular line?

misconceptions.description: Negates a slope for a perpendicular line without flipping it.

flashcard.front: Is the perpendicular slope to m just −m?
flashcard.back: No: it is −1/m.

misconceptions.description: Omits the modulus in the angle-between-lines formula, giving the obtuse angle.

flashcard.front: Why the modulus in tan θ = |(m₂ − m₁)/(1 + m₁m₂)|?
flashcard.back: Without it you may get the obtuse angle's tangent (negative).

misconceptions.description: Uses 1 − m₁m₂ in the angle-between-lines formula.

flashcard.front: Denominator of the angle-between-lines formula?
flashcard.back: 1 + m₁m₂.

misconceptions.description: Reads the slope of Ax + By + C = 0 as A/B.

flashcard.front: Slope of Ax + By + C = 0?
flashcard.back: −A ÷ B.

misconceptions.description: Omits √(A² + B²) from a distance formula.

flashcard.front: Distance between Ax + By + C₁ = 0 and Ax + By + C₂ = 0?
flashcard.back: |C₁ − C₂| ÷ √(A² + B²).

misconceptions.description: Divides by A² + B² instead of its square root.

flashcard.front: Denominator in the point–line distance formula?
flashcard.back: √(A² + B²).

misconceptions.description: Adds the constants instead of subtracting them.

flashcard.front: Parallel-line distance: |C₁ − C₂| or |C₁ + C₂|?
flashcard.back: |C₁ − C₂|, with both equations in the same form.

misconceptions.description: Writes x − y = a for equal intercepts.

flashcard.front: A line with equal intercepts a on both axes?
flashcard.back: x + y = a (slope −1).

misconceptions.description: Uses a point's coordinates as the line's intercepts.

flashcard.front: Is a point on a line the same as its intercepts?
flashcard.back: No: intercepts are where the line cuts the axes.

misconceptions.description: Multiplies magnitudes without the cosine of the angle between the vectors.

flashcard.front: a · b for vectors at angle θ?
flashcard.back: |a||b| cos θ: only the part of one vector along the other counts.

misconceptions.description: Uses sin θ in the scalar product.

flashcard.front: Scalar product: sin or cos?
flashcard.back: cos θ: a · b = |a||b| cos θ.

misconceptions.description: Reports the scalar product itself as the angle between vectors.

flashcard.front: Angle between vectors from their components?
flashcard.back: cos θ = (a · b) ÷ (|a||b|), then take the inverse cosine.

misconceptions.description: Gets the sign wrong when solving a · b = 0.

flashcard.front: Perpendicular vectors: a · b = ?
flashcard.back: 0. Solve aₓbₓ + a_yb_y = 0 carefully for the unknown.

misconceptions.description: Thinks a force perpendicular to the motion does work.

flashcard.front: Does the normal force do work on a box sliding along a level floor?
flashcard.back: No: it is perpendicular to the displacement, so W = F d cos 90° = 0.

misconceptions.description: Uses F × d for a force at an angle to the displacement.

flashcard.front: Work by a force at angle θ to the displacement?
flashcard.back: W = F d cos θ.

misconceptions.description: Uses sin θ for the work done by an angled force.

flashcard.front: Pulling at θ above the horizontal along the floor: which part does work?
flashcard.back: The horizontal part, F cos θ.

misconceptions.description: Gives the work done by friction as positive.

flashcard.front: Sign of the work done by kinetic friction on a sliding block?
flashcard.back: Negative: friction opposes the displacement.

misconceptions.description: Uses the weight instead of the friction force.

flashcard.front: Work done by friction over d?
flashcard.back: −μ N d, with μ N the friction force.

misconceptions.description: Uses a rectangle where the F–x graph is a triangle.

flashcard.front: Work from a straight F–x line rising from 0?
flashcard.back: The triangle's area, ½ F x.

misconceptions.description: Uses ½k(x₂ − x₁)² for the work stretching a spring from x₁ to x₂.

flashcard.front: Work to stretch a spring from x₁ to x₂?
flashcard.back: ½k(x₂² − x₁²), the area between x₁ and x₂ under F = kx.

misconceptions.description: Leaves out the ½ in spring work or energy.

flashcard.front: Energy stored in a spring stretched by x?
flashcard.back: ½kx²: the area of the triangle under F = kx.

misconceptions.description: Leaves out part of the area under an F–x graph.

flashcard.front: Work from an F–x graph with two parts?
flashcard.back: Add the area of every part.

misconceptions.description: Writes kinetic energy as mv².

flashcard.front: Kinetic energy?
flashcard.back: ½mv².

misconceptions.description: Forgets to square the speed in ½mv².

flashcard.front: Doubling the speed does what to KE?
flashcard.back: Multiplies it by 4: KE = ½mv².

misconceptions.description: Drops the 2 when solving Fd = ½mv² for v.

flashcard.front: Speed after work W on a body from rest?

misconceptions.description: Stops at v² and forgets the square root.

flashcard.front: From ½mv² = E, v = ?

misconceptions.description: Uses m h for gravitational potential energy.

flashcard.front: Gravitational PE gained by m raised h?
flashcard.back: mgh.

misconceptions.description: Uses centimetres directly in ½kx².

flashcard.front: Spring energy with x in cm and k in N/m?
flashcard.back: Convert x to metres first.

misconceptions.description: Leaves out the square root when finding the launch speed from a spring.

flashcard.front: Speed from a spring compressed by x?
flashcard.back: ½kx² = ½mv², so v = x√(k ÷ m).

misconceptions.description: Gives 2gh instead of √(2gh) for the speed after a fall.

flashcard.front: Speed after falling h from rest?

misconceptions.description: Uses √(gh) for the speed after a fall.

flashcard.front: mgh = ½mv² gives v = ?

misconceptions.description: Uses the whole string length as the height fallen by a pendulum.

flashcard.front: Height fallen by a pendulum released at θ?
flashcard.back: L(1 − cos θ).

misconceptions.description: Uses L cos θ as the height fallen by a pendulum.

flashcard.front: Pendulum released at θ: drop of the bob?
flashcard.back: L − L cos θ = L(1 − cos θ).

misconceptions.description: Uses the minimum speed at the top of a vertical circle for the bottom.

flashcard.front: Minimum speed at the bottom of a vertical circle on a string?
flashcard.back: √(5gR): √(gR) at the top plus the energy for the 2R climb.

misconceptions.description: Lets the speed fall to zero at the top of a vertical circle on a string.

flashcard.front: Can a body on a string be at rest at the top of a vertical circle?
flashcard.back: No: the string would go slack. It needs at least √(gR) there.

misconceptions.description: Uses m h ÷ t for the power to lift a load.

flashcard.front: Power to lift m by h in t?
flashcard.back: mgh ÷ t.

misconceptions.description: Uses F ÷ v for power.

flashcard.front: Power at constant speed against a force F?
flashcard.back: P = F v.

misconceptions.description: Divides by the time in minutes for a power in watts.

flashcard.front: A watt is a joule per …?
flashcard.back: Second. Convert minutes to seconds.

misconceptions.description: Thinks kinetic energy is conserved in every collision.

flashcard.front: Is KE conserved when two bodies stick together?
flashcard.back: No. Momentum is conserved; some KE becomes heat, sound and deformation.

misconceptions.description: Uses the sticking-collision result for an elastic collision.

flashcard.front: Elastic collision, m₁ at u hits m₂ at rest: v₂?
flashcard.back: 2m₁u ÷ (m₁ + m₂).

misconceptions.description: Thinks the struck body always moves off at the incoming speed.

flashcard.front: When does the struck ball take the full incoming speed?
flashcard.back: Only for equal masses in an elastic collision.

misconceptions.description: Gives the final kinetic energy when the loss is asked.

flashcard.front: KE lost in a collision?
flashcard.back: Initial KE − final KE.

misconceptions.description: Thinks all the kinetic energy is lost when bodies stick.

flashcard.front: Do two sticking carts stop dead?
flashcard.back: No: momentum is conserved, so they keep moving and keep some KE.
